1	# ADR-0001: Kernel Tick Driver and Frame Order
2	
3	## Status
4	Proposed
5	
6	## Date
7	2026-10-28
8	
9	## Last Verified
10	2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-1a, D.5 and `docs/engine-reference/godot/` 4.7). Engine behaviours marked UNVERIFIED below have not been run on 4.7.2.
11	
12	## Decision Makers
13	User (delegated all remaining design calls, 2026-10-28); Claude (author); reviewed by godot-specialist (engine) and technical-director (TD-ADR).
14	
15	## Summary
16	The simulation kernel needs exactly one clock, and three approved design documents still describe two different ones (the kernel's `_process`-driven `TickDriver`, and an older physics-callback tick). This ADR fixes the kernel's source: one `TickDriver` driven from the `_process` of a single always-processing host node, with a fixed per-frame order set by named process-priority constants, `tick_alpha` as the only value presentation reads from the clock, and the kernel handed to every module by injection rather than through an autoload.
17	
18	## Engine Compatibility
19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
23	| **Domain** | Core (frame loop, node processing order), with an Input boundary |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. Every API used predates the 4.3 cutoff, but the pinned engine reference is silent on cross-node `process_priority` order and on how `Engine.time_scale` scales `_process(delta)`, and 4.7 changed input device IDs. |
25	| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 → 4.7 GDScript and Input rows), `deprecated-apis.md`, `current-best-practices.md`, `modules/input.md`, `modules/physics.md` |
26	| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None. `Node._process`, `Node.process_priority`, `Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, `RefCounted`, `Engine.time_scale` and `roundi()` all exist in 4.3. |
27	| **Verification Required** | (1) Spike KRN-LAT-02: with the Input Adapter, the host node and a presentation node in one scene, the recorded `_process` call order is adapter → driver → presentation, on a dev build and on a release export. (2) `Engine.time_scale` scaling of `delta` (the kernel GDD marks it UNVERIFIED). (3) The first-frame `delta` after a long block (scene load, window drag, focus loss) is finite and handled by the cap and forgiveness, not a crash. (4) `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` fires after every `_process` in the frame (owned by ADR-0008; recorded here because the camera write depends on this order). |
28	
29	## ADR Dependencies
30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|-------|-------|
33	| **Depends On** | None (first ADR). The design source is `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-1, CR-1a and D.5. |
34	| **Enables** | ADR-0002 (command pipeline), ADR-0003 (block registry and hooks), ADR-0004 (notification and `tick_alpha` consumers), ADR-0006 (Save/Load boundary service timing), ADR-0008 (render pipeline: `present_time`, camera write), ADR-0009 (presentation subscriber contract), ADR-0019 (Input Adapter placement) |
35	| **Blocks** | Every epic that submits commands or draws from the clock: Player Controller, Pixel-Perfect Pipeline, Suit, Modular Ship Assembly (stories that quote the tick source), Interaction, Lighting. |
36	| **Ordering Note** | Do not **Accept** until the stale tick-source text is fixed in four GDDs (see § GDD sync) and spike KRN-LAT-02 has run. Authoring now is safe because this ADR follows the kernel GDD (the owner), not the stale consumers. |
37	
38	## Context
39	
40	### Problem Statement
41	The game simulates at a fixed 60 Hz in integer ticks, and everything else (render, input, audio, camera) runs at the render rate. Something has to turn engine frames into whole ticks, say when input is read relative to those ticks, and say when presentation reads the result. The kernel GDD answers this in CR-1a: a `TickDriver` with an injected delta, driven from `_process`, with the physics step "never the clock". Three consumer GDDs (Player Controller, Suit, Pixel-Perfect Pipeline) and Modular Ship Assembly still describe the physics callback as the tick source, with `physics_jitter_fix` and `max_physics_steps_per_frame` couplings. Two accumulators drifting against each other is the failure that fixed-tick determinism cannot survive, so the choice has to be recorded once, in a place stories and the control manifest will cite.
42	
43	### Constraints
44	- **Determinism (kernel H9, CR-13).** The kernel never reads wall-clock time or `delta`. Ticks are whole, and the same save bytes plus the same command stream must produce the same state hash at any render rate.
45	- **Replay and test seams.** `Kernel.step()` is a plain synchronous method. Tests call it directly or inject `delta_us` into the driver; nothing in the kernel sleeps.
46	- **Main thread only (CR-1a).** The kernel, the driver and every owner callable run on the main thread.
47	- **No physics body on any simulation path (Ship Body BDY-3).** The avatar has none, so no sim code needs the physics callback.
48	- **Latency (D.4, KRN-LAT-01/02).** Submit-to-applied within one tick on an empty queue; `L_first` median ≤ 33.3 ms, p95 ≤ 50 ms on RM-DESKTOP.
49	- **Frame budgets (ruling R12).** P99 frame ≤ 16.6 ms on RM-DESKTOP (14.9 ms with headroom) and ≤ 33.3 ms on RM-DECK (30.0 ms), release export.
50	- **Coding standard.** Dependencies are injected, not reached through singletons, so headless tests can build their own kernel.
51	- **Engine reference silent** on cross-node `process_priority` order and on `Engine.time_scale` and `delta`.
52	
53	### Requirements
54	- One tick source, and the physics callback is not it.
55	- A fixed, lint-checkable order inside one rendered frame: input sample, then the tick loop, then presentation.
56	- A catch-up cap and a forgiveness rule so a slow frame degrades to slow motion, not a spiral.
57	- A single float handed to presentation that places a drawn pose between two committed ticks.
58	- No global `Kernel` name that sim or presentation code can reach without being given it.
59	
60	## Decision
61	
62	### 1. The tick source is `_process`, in one host node
63	
64	A single `KernelHost` node (`extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`) owns a `TickDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls it from its own `_process(delta)`. The host does one thing with the engine's `delta`: it converts it once, `delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0))`, and passes the integer to the driver. That conversion and the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads in the project (kernel H9). The driver is exactly the one specified in kernel CR-1a and D.5: an integer accumulator in units of microseconds × `TICK_RATE` (`TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 per tick), a boundary service before any tick, `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)`, a re-read of the kernel state after every `step()`, lag forgiveness (`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0), result flush, and the paused service. This ADR does not restate those rules; the GDD is their authority. It records the *placement* and *order* decisions below.
65	
66	**The physics callback is not the clock and is not used by any simulation or presentation code in the MVP.** No script in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/` defines `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces`; `physics_interpolation` stays off; `physics_jitter_fix` and `max_physics_steps_per_frame` are left at engine defaults and nothing is coupled to them. A later Vertical Slice physics projection (ADR-0033) runs in `_physics_process` as a read-only PROJECTOR and never steps the kernel.
67	
68	### 2. Frame order is fixed by named priority constants
69	
70	Godot runs `_process` in ascending `process_priority`, ties broken by tree order. Tree order is not a contract we want to depend on, so the order is fixed by three constants in one file, `src/kernel/process_priority.gd`:
71	
72	```gdscript
73	class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted
74	
75	## Lower values run first inside one rendered frame.
76	const INPUT_ADAPTER: int = -100   # INPUT_SURFACE objects only; samples input, calls submit()
77	const TICK_DRIVER: int = -50      # KernelHost: boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, result flush
78	const PRESENTATION: int = 0       # engine default; every presentation node, so a node that forgets to set it still runs after the driver
79	```
80	
81	The three-step order is therefore **input adapter → tick driver → presentation**, matching the kernel GDD's priority table (its ordinals 0, 1 and 2 are order only; the values above are the implementation). Choosing `PRESENTATION` as the engine default is deliberate: an unset node lands after the driver, which is the safe failure.
82	
83	Rules, each of which becomes a lint (ADR-0010):
84	- A node whose `process_priority` is below `TICK_DRIVER` must be a registered INPUT_SURFACE object. Nothing else may run before the driver.
85	- No node other than `KernelHost` may use `TICK_DRIVER`'s value.
86	- A presentation node's `process_priority` is `PRESENTATION` or greater and is never set to a literal; it references the constant.
87	
88	### 3. The Input Adapter samples and submits in its own `_process`
89	
90	The Adapter (an INPUT_SURFACE, Player Controller GDD PC-1(a)) reads device state and calls `submit()` from its `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`. It may latch raw events in `_input`/`_unhandled_input`, which the engine delivers before the frame's `_process` calls, but it submits only from `_process`. Its commands are therefore queued before the driver's boundary service and tick loop run, so an intent sampled in frame N sits in tick T's P1 batch, is applied in P2 and is integrated in P3 of the same tick: one tick of latency, never two. The Adapter never samples in `_physics_process`. Devices are identified by event type, not by `device == 0` (4.7 changed mouse and keyboard device IDs; ADR-0019).
91	
92	In a frame that runs several ticks (catch-up), the Adapter has submitted once, so only the first tick of that frame sees new commands. Continuing movement survives because intent state lives in `controller.state` and commands are edge- or change-based, not per-tick.
93	
94	### 4. `tick_alpha` is the only clock value presentation reads
95	
96	At the end of each driver frame the driver publishes `tick_alpha = clamp(acc / TICK_UNITS, 0.0, 1.0)` (identical to kernel D.3's `t_since_last_commit / tick_duration`). It is a presentation-only float: it is not a state block, is never hashed or saved, and the simulation never reads it. Presentation reads it once per frame in its `_process` and interpolates previous-to-current committed state with `pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) * tick_alpha)` (Pipeline PR-5). Because forgiveness at `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0 drops whole lag ticks at the end of every frame but keeps the sub-tick remainder, `acc < TICK_UNITS` after the driver runs, so `tick_alpha` is continuous and stays in [0, 1) in normal operation and is held at 1 (not extrapolated) only transiently.
97	
98	Presentation also keeps a render-rate cosmetic clock, `present_time`, owned by the Pipeline root (PR-21, ADR-0008). The rule recorded here: **cosmetic phase (flicker, gutter, fades) uses `present_time`; anything the simulation also computes (beacon aim, poses, wane) uses the kernel tick; the tick counter is never used for cosmetic phase** (Lighting LO-4).
99	
100	### 5. The kernel reaches modules by injection
101	
102	There is no `Kernel` autoload and no static singleton for kernel or game state. The main scene's root script (the **composition root**, `src/game/game.gd`) constructs the kernel, the `TickDriver` and the `KernelHost`, then passes the kernel to every module and subscriber through `setup(kernel: Kernel)`. A module stores the reference it was given. Headless tests construct their own `Kernel` (and a `TickDriver` with a fake `delta_us`) and need no scene. In the code examples in `docs/architecture/architecture.md`, `Kernel.` reads as "the injected kernel". There are no recorded exceptions.
103	
104	### 6. Pause, load and the tree
105	
106	The kernel's `PAUSED` state is the only pause the simulation knows (kernel CR-16). The MVP never sets `SceneTree.paused`; `KernelHost` is `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` regardless, so it keeps running through the boundary service even if a future change pauses the tree. Window focus loss, an OS-level stall or a long load simply produces one large `delta`: the cap (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4) and forgiveness absorb it, and the accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`, so loads, saves and pauses never cause catch-up bursts afterwards (kernel CR-1a).
107	
108	### Architecture Diagram
109	
110	```
111	Engine main loop, one rendered frame (_process in ascending process_priority)
112	│
113	├─ -100  Input Adapter           [INPUT_SURFACE]   reads input → kernel.submit(...)           (queued only)
114	│
115	├─  -50  KernelHost._process(delta)
116	│          delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta × 1e6))                  ← the only wall-clock read
117	│          TickDriver.frame(delta_us):
118	│            1 boundary service (SAVING/LOADING/pause/resume; may clear acc, discard this frame's delta)
119	│            2 repeat ticks_run times, re-reading kernel state after each:
120	│                 Kernel.step() = P0 begin · P1 intake · P2 dispatch · P3 step hooks · P4 commit · P5 notify · P6 boundary
121	│            3 forgiveness (drop whole lag ticks, keep the sub-tick remainder)
122	│            4 flush the result buffer
123	│            5 if PAUSED: paused service
124	│          tick_alpha = clamp(acc / TICK_UNITS, 0, 1)
125	│
126	└─   0   Presentation nodes      [PRESENTATION]    handlers already marked dirty at P5;
127	           (Pipeline root, Avatar Presenter, Lighting, Trail,        draw from committed views at tick_alpha;
128	            Instruments, HUD, Audio, Debug)                          Pipeline writes camera in frame_pre_draw
129	
130	_physics_process: not used by the kernel, simulation or presentation in the MVP.
131	```
132	
133	### Key Interfaces
134	
135	```gdscript
136	class_name TickDriver extends RefCounted
137	## Turns an injected wall-time delta into whole kernel ticks. No scene tree, no engine clock.
138	func _init(kernel: Kernel, params: TickParams) -> void
139	func frame(delta_us: int) -> TickFrameResult   # boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, flush; returns ticks_run, dropped, tick_alpha
140	var tick_alpha: float:                         # presentation-only; read once per frame
141		get: return _tick_alpha
142	
143	class_name KernelHost extends Node
144	func setup(driver: TickDriver) -> void         # called by the composition root; sets process_mode and process_priority
145	func _process(delta: float) -> void            # delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0)); driver.frame(delta_us)
146	
147	class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted  # constants shown in Decision § 2
148	
149	# Every module and subscriber:
150	func setup(kernel: Kernel) -> void             # injected; stored; never looked up through a global
151	```
152	
153	### Implementation Guidelines
154	- **Must** drive `Kernel.step()` only from `TickDriver.frame()`, and call `TickDriver.frame()` only from `KernelHost._process`. Tests may call either directly.
155	- **Must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/`; **must never** set `SceneTree.paused` in the MVP.
156	- **Must** use the `ProcessPriority` constants; **must never** write a literal `process_priority` value.
157	- **Must** submit input only from the Input Adapter's `_process`; **must never** call `submit()` from `_input`, `_physics_process` or a signal handler.
158	- **Must** pass the kernel in with `setup(kernel)`; **must never** add an autoload, a static variable or a group lookup that exposes the kernel, a block or a read view.
159	- **Must** read `tick_alpha` in presentation only, never in a simulation callable, and **must never** use the tick counter for cosmetic animation phase.
160	- **Must** keep `Engine.time_scale = 1.0` in release builds; a boot check records `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` in diagnostics otherwise.
161	- **Must** keep the `delta_us` conversion in `KernelHost` and nowhere else; the lint for forbidden clock APIs (`Time.get_ticks_*`, `OS.get_ticks_*`, `get_process_delta_time`) allow-lists only `KernelHost` and the diagnostics timer.
162	- **Should** test the driver with injected `delta_us` sequences (16,000 / 16,667 / 17,334 µs patterns, 100 ms hitches, zero-length frames) and the frame order with a recording scene (KRN-LAT-01, KRN-LAT-02).
163	
164	## Alternatives Considered
165	
166	### Alternative 1: Drive the tick from the physics callback
167	- **Description**: `Kernel.step()` runs in `_physics_process` at `physics_ticks_per_second` = 60, with `max_physics_steps_per_frame` set equal to `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` and `physics_jitter_fix` set to 0. The Adapter samples input in the same callback. This is what the Player Controller, Suit, Pipeline and Assembly GDDs still describe.
168	- **Pros**: The engine already owns an accumulator and catch-up; Godot Physics 2D steps align with the tick if a physics projection is added later.
169	- **Cons**: Two accumulators (the engine's and the kernel's D.5) must agree, and `physics_jitter_fix` smooths the engine's delta, which silently changes tick spacing unless forced to 0. The coupling to `max_physics_steps_per_frame` is an engine setting a mis-edit can break without any test noticing. Input is sampled in a callback that may run zero or two times per rendered frame, making latency irregular. The reference is silent on the 4.7 behaviour of all three settings. The MVP has no physics body, so there is nothing for the physics step to align with.
170	- **Rejection Reason**: The kernel GDD rejected it in CR-1a for these reasons, and the kernel is the owner. It adds an unverified engine dependency to a layer whose whole point is that nothing outside it can change tick behaviour.
171	
172	### Alternative 2: Own accumulator from `Time.get_ticks_usec()`
173	- **Description**: The driver reads the wall clock directly each frame and accumulates real elapsed microseconds, ignoring the engine's `delta`.
174	- **Pros**: Exact integer microseconds, no float conversion; unaffected by `Engine.time_scale`.
175	- **Cons**: A second wall-clock read, which breaks the "one conversion, one diagnostics timer" rule (H9) and makes the clock lint much harder; bypasses the engine's own frame pacing (a debugger break or breakpoint would produce a huge catch-up burst immediately); and removes the dev-build ability to scale simulated speed through `time_scale`.
176	- **Rejection Reason**: The float conversion of `delta` is exact enough (a double carries the full range of a frame to well under a microsecond) and keeps a single, injectable time input. Held as the fallback if the spike finds `delta` unusable.
177	
178	### Alternative 3: A dedicated simulation thread
179	- **Description**: The kernel ticks on its own thread at a fixed rate and presentation reads snapshots.
180	- **Pros**: Simulation cost cannot stall rendering.
181	- **Cons**: Violates the main-thread rule (CR-1a), makes owner callables and read views thread-unsafe, and would need synchronisation across every block. The kernel budget (P3 ≤ 2.0 ms) does not need it.
182	- **Rejection Reason**: Complexity and determinism risk with no budget case for it.
183	
184	### Alternative 4: Autoload `Kernel` singleton (for access)
185	- **Description**: Register the kernel as an autoload so any script can call `Kernel.submit(...)` or `Kernel.tick_alpha`.
186	- **Pros**: Least typing; the examples in the architecture document already read this way.
187	- **Cons**: Every module gains a hidden dependency; headless tests must reset a global between cases; two kernels (replay comparison, MIRROR in VS-B) cannot coexist in one process; contradicts the coding standard.
188	- **Rejection Reason**: Injection costs one `setup()` call per module and keeps the kernel constructible by tests and, later, a second instance for MIRROR.
189	
190	## Consequences
191	
192	### Positive
193	- One clock, one place it is read, and one stated order inside a frame; the tick-source disagreement across four GDDs is resolved in favour of the owner.
194	- Tests run the kernel and driver with no scene tree and an injected `delta_us`, so replay-at-any-frame-rate (TR-pxl-022) is a cheap, deterministic test.
195	- The sampled-input latency is bounded and regular (one tick), unlike a physics-callback sample.
196	- Defaults are safe failures: an unset presentation priority runs after the driver; an unset physics setting is irrelevant.
197	- Injection lets a second kernel (MIRROR, replay comparison) exist in one process.
198	
199	### Negative
200	- The order rests on `process_priority` behaving as documented across unrelated nodes, which the pinned reference does not state (spike KRN-LAT-02). If it does not, the fallback is a single parent node that calls the Adapter, driver and presentation in explicit sequence.
201	- Every module needs a `setup(kernel)` call and the composition root grows with the module count; forgetting one fails at first use, so a boot check lists modules that were never given a kernel.
202	- Float conversion of `delta` adds a ≤ 0.5 µs rounding per frame; it does not accumulate into the tick count, because the accumulator is integer, but replay tests must inject `delta_us` rather than real frames.
203	- A frame that runs several ticks submits input once, so only its first tick sees new commands; this is correct for change-based commands but must be remembered when writing tick-level tests.
204	
205	## Risks
206	- **`process_priority` order across nodes behaves differently than assumed.** Mitigation: KRN-LAT-02 runs before acceptance, on dev and release builds; the sequential-parent fallback is described above.
207	- **`Engine.time_scale` scales `delta` differently in 4.7.2.** Mitigation: pinned to 1.0 in release, flagged `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` otherwise; verified in the spike.
208	- **A consumer GDD's stale text is implemented instead of this ADR.** Mitigation: the four GDDs are fixed before acceptance (§ GDD sync) and a lint rejects `_physics_process` in `src/kernel`, `src/sim` and `src/presentation`.
209	- **Large `delta` after an OS stall produces one slow-motion burst.** Mitigation: cap and forgiveness bound it to four ticks, and the accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`.
210	- **The Pipeline's camera write in `frame_pre_draw` may precede some `_process` calls.** Mitigation: owned by ADR-0008 and pipeline spike step 11; presentation reads committed state, so the camera is allowed to use the previous frame's pose if the order proves unreliable.
211	
212	## GDD Requirements Addressed
213	
214	| GDD System | Requirement | How This ADR Addresses It |
215	|------------|-------------|--------------------------|
216	| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-1, CR-1a: fixed 60 Hz tick; `TickDriver` with injected delta driven from `_process` by one always-processing node; physics step is not the clock (TR-cmd-001, TR-cmd-002) | Decision § 1 adopts it verbatim and names the host node and the one `delta` conversion |
217	| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-1a priority table: input adapter, then driver, then presentation, with a lint on `process_priority` (TR-cmd-004) | Decision § 2 fixes the constants and the three lint rules |
218	| command-simulation-layer.md | D.5: lag dropped at end of frame, accumulator cleared on every transition into `RUNNING` (TR-cmd-003) | Decision § 1 and § 6 reference it; the `tick_alpha` derivation in § 4 depends on its remainder rule |
219	| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-1a main thread only; no `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` or `call_deferred` into kernel code (TR-cmd-005) | Implementation Guidelines; Alternative 3 rejected |
220	| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-2: per-tick phases P0–P6 (TR-cmd-006) | Architecture Diagram shows where the phases sit in the frame |
221	| player-controller-input.md | PC-1(a), PC-15: the Adapter samples and submits before the kernel steps; one tick latency (TR-pc-004) | Decision § 3: Adapter samples in its own `_process` at `INPUT_ADAPTER`; the GDD's "physics callback" wording is stale (§ GDD sync) |
222	| pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md | PR-21, PR-22: sim stays 60 Hz at any render rate; `present_time`; tick-before-render ordering; tick-driver ownership (TR-pxl-021, TR-pxl-022) | Decision § 1, § 4 and § 6; the `physics_jitter_fix` / `max_physics_steps_per_frame` clauses are removed by the GDD fix |
223	| 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md | LO-4: kernel clock for what the sim also computes, `present_time` for cosmetic phase (TR-light-008) | Decision § 4 records the rule |
224	| hud-and-suit-layer.md, chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md | Presentation reads committed state at render rate and never causes a tick (TR-hud-010, TR-charttable-005) | Decision § 4 and the Architecture Diagram |
225	| derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md | P3 budget wording tied to the frame step (TR-derelict-021) | The tick loop is the one place P3 cost is incurred; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` semantics are fixed with ADR-0003 (IC-4) |
226	
227	## Performance Implications
228	- **CPU**: The driver itself is an integer add, a divide and a loop; it is negligible against the kernel's budgets (P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99; frame simulation ≤ 4.0 ms for one tick and ≤ 6.0 ms for four), which are measured on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK. At 30 fps (RM-DECK) a frame normally runs two ticks; the 4-tick cap means slow motion begins below 15 fps.
229	- **Memory**: One `TickDriver`, one `KernelHost` node, a few integers. No per-frame allocation in the driver (`TickFrameResult` is reused).
230	- **Load Time**: None. The accumulator is cleared when load finishes, so load time is not repaid as ticks.
231	- **Network**: None at MVP. In VS-B a MIRROR kernel uses the same driver with no authority over commands (ADR-0002, ADR-0032).
232	
233	## Migration Plan
234	There is no code yet. The change is to documents: fix the stale tick-source text in the Player Controller, Suit, Pixel-Perfect Pipeline and Modular Ship Assembly GDDs (list below) before this ADR is Accepted, and replace the `Kernel.` global in architecture-document examples when the document is next revised (it already says "the injected kernel").
235	
236	## Validation Criteria
237	- KRN-LAT-01 passes: with an injected driver fed 16,000 / 16,667 / 17,334 µs frames, `L_first` never exceeds `2 × frame_duration + L_present`.
238	- KRN-LAT-02 passes on a dev build and on a release export: the recorded call order is adapter → driver → presentation, and the lint finds no presentation node at or below `TICK_DRIVER`.
239	- A scripted 10-second replay produces an identical `state_hash` at `max_fps` 30, 60, 144 and 0 (TR-pxl-022) with no `physics_*` settings touched.
240	- A grep of `src/kernel`, `src/sim` and `src/presentation` finds no `_physics_process`, no `SceneTree.paused` write, no literal `process_priority` value and no `Kernel` autoload.
241	- A 100 ms hitch produces four ticks, drops the rest and leaves `acc` below one tick; a load, save or pause does not produce catch-up ticks after returning to `RUNNING`.
242	
243	## GDD sync (stale tick-source text — to fix before Acceptance)
244	The kernel GDD (owner) is correct. These consumer passages still describe the physics callback and conflict with this ADR:
245	- `design/gdd/player-controller-input.md` L62 (PC-1(a)), L740 and L751 (latency terms), L1021 (Immediacy), L1077 (AC-PCI-003: "in the same physics callback")
246	- `design/gdd/suit-and-equipment.md` L1441
247	- `design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` L227, L297, L1219 (`physics_jitter_fix`, `max_physics_steps_per_frame`, "two accumulators")
248	- `design/gdd/modular-ship-assembly.md` L1058, L1161, L1593, L1772 (the "when the tick is driven by the physics callback" conditions and the boot assertion)
249	
250	## Related
251	- `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` (CR-1, CR-1a, CR-2, D.3, D.4, D.5; KRN-LAT-01..03; open question 2 closed by CR-1a)
252	- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` (§ Data Flow 1, OQ-1, OQ-13)
253	- ADR-0002, ADR-0003, ADR-0004, ADR-0008, ADR-0009, ADR-0010, ADR-0019 (to be written)
254	- Review rulings: delegated ruling G1 (owner wins)

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude-artifacts
Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. Call guide before the first publish of a session: it holds the rules a page must meet. This server cannot change who can see an artifact (sharing, publishing to the web, unsharing), delete an artifact or read view counts; say so instead of calling a tool. # Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,

  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or

### 8. Initialisation order

```
1. Engine boot; project.godot guard rails asserted (stretch, filters, snap, hdr_2d, physics_interpolation off)
2. Pipeline root builds the viewport stack (BOOTING → PRESENTING)
3. Content data loads in a fixed order: Item DB → section templates (manifest order) → world records,
   verb tables, tuning tables; boot lints and invariant assertions (refuse the build on failure)
4. Kernel BOOTING: owners register blocks, command types, hooks, binding sources, diagnostics channels
   (Layout, Graph last of the Item DB → Layout → Graph chain; then Body, Controller, Emitter, Suit,
   Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror, Sanity). Registration then freezes; hook topo-sort.
5. Presentation subscribers subscribe (Lighting, Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, PROJECTORs, Debug)
6. Main menu (Chart Table) → New Game: Save/Load new_game(seed) → kernel request_new_game(seed, 0)
   → Web Map init_world inside one WriteScope: Layout build_section → Emitter instantiate_section_emitters
   → Interaction sync_section → PROJECTOR notification → initial NEW_GAME generation written
   or Continue: load path (§ 7)
```

---

## API Boundaries

Signatures are GDScript (typed). They restate the GDD contracts at the boundary; the GDD anchor in brackets is the authority.

### Kernel ingress and registration [command-simulation-layer CR-4..CR-10, CR-19]

```gdscript
# Ingress (INPUT_SURFACE handle only). Fire-and-forget: returns nothing, calls nothing.
func submit(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, actor: int = NO_ACTOR, correlation: int = 0) -> void
# SYSTEM-origin submission from a step hook or apply (dedupe optional).
func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void

# Registration — legal only in BOOTING, frozen afterwards; violations fail boot.
func register_block(desc: BlockDescriptor) -> void       # block_id, owner, schema_version, class, persist,
                                                          # persist_scope, scope, gameplay, interpolated,
                                                          # repl_hint, restore_after, callables
func register_command(desc: CommandTypeDescriptor) -> void  # allowed_origins, actor_binding, actor_source,
                                                          # coalesce, max_age_ticks, allowed_when_paused, writes_blocks
func register_hook(hook_id: StringName, owner: Object, divisor: int, offset: int,
		after: Array[StringName], tolerates_stale: Array[StringName]) -> void
func subscribe(cls: SubscriberClass, handler: Callable) -> SubscriptionHandle
```

**Invariants callers respect:** never construct a command with `issuer_peer`; payloads hold only whitelisted Variant types (finite floats, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 4 KiB, no Object/Callable/NodePath/RID); never submit from a PRESENTATION handler. **Kernel guarantees:** exactly one terminal result per command; apply order ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`; subscribers see only post-P4 state.

### Owner-callable contract [CR-19, ruling R3]

```gdscript
# Every kernel-invoked owner callable receives a ctx and returns only ctx.complete().
func validate(cmd: Command, views: ReadViews, ctx: ApplyContext) -> CompletionToken:
	if not _target_exists(cmd.payload):
		ctx.reject(&"NO_SUCH_TARGET")
		return ctx.complete()
	ctx.ok()
	return ctx.complete()

func apply(cmd: Command, scope: WriteScope, ctx: ApplyContext) -> CompletionToken
func snapshot(ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken           # ctx.put(plain_dictionary)
func restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken

If they are registered `Callable`s on `RefCounted` owners, the rule is moot and GDScript's ordinary "a typed function returns on every path" check applies. ADR-0003 chooses one (base class or registered Callables). Either way the kernel checks the returned token's identity with a real `if`, never an `assert`, because `assert` is stripped from release exports (KRN-CTX-06). Verified against `docs/engine-reference/godot/breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 → 4.7 (GDScript). Behaviour confirmed: NEEDS VERIFICATION on a release export.

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

**TR Registry:** `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
- Stable requirement IDs (e.g. `TR-movement-001`) that link GDD requirements to stories
- Never renumber existing IDs — only append new ones
- Updated by `/architecture-review` Phase 8

**Control Manifest:** `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`
- Flat programmer rules sheet: Required / Forbidden / Guardrails per layer
- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header
- Stories embed this version; `/story-done` checks for staleness

**Validation:** Run `/architecture-review` after completing a set of ADRs.

## Engine Reference (`docs/engine-reference/`)

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

250	## Data Flow
251	
252	### 1. Frame update path
253	
254	One rendered frame. The tick is driven from `_process`, never from the physics callback (kernel CR-1a; see Open Question OQ-1 for three GDDs that still cite the physics callback).
255	
256	```
257	Engine frame (_process order by process_priority)
258	│
259	├─ priority 0  Input Adapter (INPUT_SURFACE; the only presentation-side node below the driver's priority, so the KRN-LAT-02 priority lint exempts INPUT_SURFACE nodes)
260	│     read InputMap actions → change-only intents (set_move_intent, set_aim ≤ every 3 ticks)
261	│     → kernel.submit(type, payload, actor, correlation)            [sync call, queued]
262	│
263	├─ priority 1  TickDriver (the only wall-clock reader)
264	│     accumulator += delta_us × TICK_RATE ; ticks = min(floor(acc / 1e6), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME=4)
265	│     boundary service (P6 work deferred from last frame: SAVING / LOADING)
266	│     repeat ticks times: Kernel.step()  ──► P0 Begin
267	│                                           P1 Intake   (queue → this tick's batch, coalesce intents)
268	│                                           P2 Dispatch (authority check → validate → apply in WriteScope)
269	│                                           P3 Step     (hooks whose T mod divisor == offset, topo order)
270	│                                           P4 Commit
271	│                                           P5 Notify   (batches queued; PRESENTATION merged per frame)
272	│                                           P6 Boundary (snapshot/restore/pause requests)
273	│     drop lag (LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS 0) ; flush results ; compute tick_alpha
274	│
275	└─ priority 2  Presentation subscribers (render callback)
276	      handlers only mark dirty → draw using read views at tick_alpha:
277	      pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) × tick_alpha)
278	      Avatar Presenter → Lighting → Trail → Instruments (perceived()) → HUD (perceived()) → Audio
279	      Pipeline root: CameraSolver → canvas_transform in frame_pre_draw
280	```
281	
282	**P3 hook schedule (MVP).** Divisor and offset decide which ticks a hook runs on; `after:` orders hooks that run on the same tick. An `after:` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick should declare `tolerates_stale` (CR-3); an undeclared one boots with a warning (ruling R-8), so the warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run.
283	
284	| Hook | Owner | Divisor | Offset | After |
285	|---|---|---|---|---|
286	| `controller.step` | Controller | 1 | 0 | `suit.vitals` (stale-tolerant) |
287	| `layout.doors` | Layout | 1 | 0 | — |
288	| `body.integrate` | Body | 1 | 0 | `controller.step`, `layout.doors` |
289	| `controller.noise` | Controller | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate` |
290	| `emitter.place` | Emitter | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate`, `graph.propagate.failure` (stale-tolerant) |
291	| `interaction.step` | Interaction | 1 | 0 | `emitter.place` |
292	| `assembly.step` | Assembly | 1 | 0 | `interaction.step` |
293	| `transit.step` | Web Map | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate`, `graph.propagate.failure` (**undeclared** stale edge, IC-11) |
294	| `graph.propagate.power` | Graph | 6 | 0 | — |
295	| `graph.propagate.atmo` | Graph | 6 | 2 | `graph.propagate.power` (stale-tolerant) |
296	| `graph.propagate.failure` | Graph | 6 | 4 | `graph.propagate.atmo` (stale-tolerant) |
297	| `suit.vitals` | Suit | 6 | 2 | `graph.propagate.atmo` |
298	| `attention.step` | Attention | 6 | 0 | `graph.propagate.power`, `emitter.place` |

302	The kernel builds this order once in BOOTING; an unknown `after:` id or a cycle fails boot. ADR-0003 records the sort; each owning GDD remains the authority on its own row.

304	**Budgets (P99, release export, RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK):** P3 ≤ 2.0 ms (alarm at `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 ms); frame simulation ≤ 4.0 ms for one tick and ≤ 6.0 ms for four; Graph hooks ≤ 0.5 ms on a hook tick; `emitter.place` + exposure ≤ 0.4 ms; Sanity median ≤ 0.5 ms; pipeline `_process` ≤ 0.5 ms; light CPU ≤ 1.0 ms steady; total frame ≤ 14.9 ms desktop and ≤ 30.0 ms Deck (90 % of the 16.6 / 33.3 ms ceilings, ruling R12).

420	## API Boundaries
421	
422	Signatures are GDScript (typed). They restate the GDD contracts at the boundary; the GDD anchor in brackets is the authority.
423	
424	### Kernel ingress and registration [command-simulation-layer CR-4..CR-10, CR-19]
425	
426	```gdscript
427	# Ingress (INPUT_SURFACE handle only). Fire-and-forget: returns nothing, calls nothing.
428	func submit(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, actor: int = NO_ACTOR, correlation: int = 0) -> void
429	# SYSTEM-origin submission from a step hook or apply (dedupe optional).
430	func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
431	
432	# Registration — legal only in BOOTING, frozen afterwards; violations fail boot.
433	func register_block(desc: BlockDescriptor) -> void       # block_id, owner, schema_version, class, persist,
434	                                                          # persist_scope, scope, gameplay, interpolated,
435	                                                          # repl_hint, restore_after, callables
436	func register_command(desc: CommandTypeDescriptor) -> void  # allowed_origins, actor_binding, actor_source,
437	                                                          # coalesce, max_age_ticks, allowed_when_paused, writes_blocks
438	func register_hook(hook_id: StringName, owner: Object, divisor: int, offset: int,
439			after: Array[StringName], tolerates_stale: Array[StringName]) -> void
440	func subscribe(cls: SubscriberClass, handler: Callable) -> SubscriptionHandle
441	```
442	
443	**Invariants callers respect:** never construct a command with `issuer_peer`; payloads hold only whitelisted Variant types (finite floats, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 4 KiB, no Object/Callable/NodePath/RID); never submit from a PRESENTATION handler. **Kernel guarantees:** exactly one terminal result per command; apply order ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`; subscribers see only post-P4 state.
444	
445	### Owner-callable contract [CR-19, ruling R3]
446	
447	```gdscript
448	# Every kernel-invoked owner callable receives a ctx and returns only ctx.complete().
449	func validate(cmd: Command, views: ReadViews, ctx: ApplyContext) -> CompletionToken:
450		if not _target_exists(cmd.payload):
451			ctx.reject(&"NO_SUCH_TARGET")
452			return ctx.complete()
453		ctx.ok()
454		return ctx.complete()
455	
456	func apply(cmd: Command, scope: WriteScope, ctx: ApplyContext) -> CompletionToken
457	func snapshot(ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken           # ctx.put(plain_dictionary)
458	func restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken
459	func post_restore(ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken
460	func read_view(ctx: Object) -> CompletionToken
461	```
462	
463	⚠️ `CompletionToken` return — Godot 4.7 (post-cutoff; HIGH only if owners are subclasses). The 4.7 rule (an override of a typed method inherits its return type and needs an explicit `return`) applies **only if** owner callables override a base class such as `BlockOwner`. If they are registered `Callable`s on `RefCounted` owners, the rule is moot and GDScript's ordinary "a typed function returns on every path" check applies. ADR-0003 chooses one (base class or registered Callables). Either way the kernel checks the returned token's identity with a real `if`, never an `assert`, because `assert` is stripped from release exports (KRN-CTX-06). Verified against `docs/engine-reference/godot/breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 → 4.7 (GDScript). Behaviour confirmed: NEEDS VERIFICATION on a release export.

474	func rebase_on_attach(scope: WriteScope, surviving: int, absorbed: int, frame_shift_px: Vector2i) -> int  # OK or -FAULT_CODE

701	## Architecture Principles
702	
703	1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
704	2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
705	3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
706	4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
707	5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
708	6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

11:> **Design Review (2026-10-27)**: first formal review — 4 BLOCKING findings and the RECOMMENDED batch applied in this revision (fault channel CR-19, result identity and delivery CR-5, tick driver CR-1a and D.5, ratification register). **Ratification (2026-10-27 — user ruling, design-review decisions)**: the user ratified R-1..R-20 as written (Open Question 18 records it) and set the lag-forgiveness policy to `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0` (Open Question 19); every *(adopted — decision log)* and *(proposed)* marker is cleared and the ratified text is binding. The CD approval above (2026-10-25) predates these amendments and this ratification and has not been re-run. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
58:*Rationale and alternatives.* The gameplay-programmer argued for a 20 Hz kernel (slow systems don't need more; worst-case 50 ms latency is invisible behind immediate local acknowledgement) but set a hard floor of 15 Hz and would push back at 10. The engine-programmer argued for tick = physics rate so the moving ship body and the characters inside it share one timeline (*historical*: CR-1a later settled that the tick is driven from `_process`, not the physics step, and Body integrates ship-local kinematics inside the sim, so physics alignment is no longer a reason for any `TICK_RATE`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. 60 Hz + divisors satisfies both: one clock, submit-to-applied within one tick (16.7 ms of simulated time) on an empty queue, and the cost profile of a 10 Hz graph. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A variable timestep was rejected (breaks replay, tests and save equivalence); a 30 Hz kernel sits at a 2:1 ratio to the 60 fps render rate (alternate frames run 0 and 1 ticks), not at an awkward one to the physics step, which is not the clock. The tick *source* is settled in CR-1a (a `TickDriver` with an injected delta, not the physics callback); `step()` stays a plain method that tests and a future server call directly. Changing `TICK_RATE` later invalidates every tuned value expressed in ticks. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
60:**CR-1a. Tick driver, clock source and catch-up** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; closes former Open Question 2, the technical-director confirms it in the spike)*. `Kernel.step()` has no clock. A `TickDriver` (a `RefCounted`, no scene tree) owns the accumulator, receives time as an injected integer count of microseconds (`delta_us`), and is driven by exactly one node with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` from its `_process(delta)`; that node converts the engine's `delta` to `delta_us` once, and that conversion plus the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads in the project (H9). **Godot's physics step is not the clock**: at MVP the avatar has no physics body (CR-13), so nothing needs the physics callback, and the driver needs no coupling to `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame` (the former coupled constraint 4 is deleted). A later Vertical Slice physics projection runs in `_physics_process` as a `PROJECTOR` reading committed state and never steps the kernel. The accumulator is an integer in units of *microseconds × TICK_RATE*, so one tick is exactly `TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 units for every integer `TICK_RATE` (no float drift, no boundary flips); each frame that begins (after the boundary service) with the kernel `RUNNING` adds `acc += delta_us × TICK_RATE`. **Order of the add against the clear** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the boundary service runs first; if it moved the kernel into `RUNNING` (a resume, a load, a finished save) the accumulator is cleared and **that frame's own `delta_us` is discarded** — the frame runs 0 ticks, because its wall time was spent paused, loading or saving — and the add applies from the next frame on; a frame that finds the kernel not `RUNNING` adds nothing. Per frame the driver (1) runs the boundary service (CR-15) before any tick; (2) while the kernel is `RUNNING`, runs `step()` `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)` times, **re-reading the kernel state after every `step()`** and stopping (and clearing `acc`) the moment it is no longer `RUNNING` — a P6 pause, a restore, a fault; (3) applies lag forgiveness (D.5); (4) flushes the result buffer (CR-5); (5) while `PAUSED`, runs the paused boundary service (CR-16). **The accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`** (from `LOADING`, `PAUSED` or `SAVING`), so a load, an autosave or a pause never produces catch-up ticks afterwards. | L_wait | float | 0–`2 × frame_duration` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: widened from one frame)* | calculated | Wall time from submit to the frame whose driver step runs tick `queued_tick + 1` — ≈ 0 when the event is handled before that frame's driver `_process` (the input adapter runs at step 0, CR-1a) and that frame runs a tick; up to one frame when it arrives after the driver (or from a P5 handler); **up to two frames when the next frame is a 0-tick frame** — at 60 fps against a 60 Hz tick the accumulator phase makes 0-tick and 2-tick frames routine, not exceptional (a frame fractionally shorter than a tick runs none) |
| (apply_tick − queued_tick − 1) × tick_duration_wall | float | 0–116.7 ms | calculated | Backlog term: 0 for an empty queue (`apply_tick − queued_tick == 1`); 0 wall time for ticks run inside a catch-up frame |
| frame_duration | float | 16.7 ms at 60 fps; 33.3 at 30 fps | calculated (engine) | Render frame period |
| L_present | float | 0–`frame_duration` | calculated | From the P5 commit to the end of the frame that draws it; presentation runs after the driver in the same frame (CR-1a), so this is the rest of that frame, not an additional one |
| tick_duration_wall | float | 16.7 ms | calculated | Interpolation term: presentation draws `prev + (curr − prev) × tick_alpha`, so the first drawn frame shows a fraction of the change and the full committed value is drawn one tick later |
| L_first / L_full | float | see below | calculated | Submit → first changed frame / submit → full committed value drawn (excludes display scan-out) |

**Output Range (60 Hz tick, 60 fps render, driver ahead of presentation within the frame):** **Empty queue, typical (no 0-tick frame in the path): `L_first` < 33.3 ms** (< 16.7 ms of waiting for the tick plus < 16.7 ms to the end of the drawing frame), **`L_full` < 50 ms**. **Empty queue, worst case (a 0-tick frame in the path, `L_wait` up to two frames): `L_first` < 50 ms, `L_full` < 66.7 ms** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; derived from the widened `L_wait`, not a new target: the 33.3 / 50 ms figures are the typical bound and the Game Feel target, the 50 / 66.7 ms figures the worst-case bound the percentile AC gates on)*. **Backlogged queue:** add `(apply_tick − queued_tick − 1) × 16.7 ms`, up to +116.7 ms at a full queue (`apply_tick − queued_tick == 8`). At 30 fps render the empty-queue `L_first` is < 66.7 ms. Immediate *acknowledgement* (CR-4) is presentation's and is 0 ticks by construction. These are the only latency bounds in this GDD: CR-1's 'within one tick' is the simulated-time component (`apply_tick − queued_tick == 1`), the 33.3 ms figure in Game Feel is `L_first`, and the interpolation term makes `L_full` a tick longer. The engine reference is silent on `_process` ordering between nodes, so the 'same frame' path is verified by the spike.
**Example:** Press at 2 ms into frame k, before the driver's `_process` at 3 ms: the tick runs at ≈ 3 ms, P5 at ≈ 4 ms, the frame is drawn when it ends at 16.7 ms → `L_first` ≈ 14.7 ms (`L_wait` ≈ 1, `L_present` ≈ 13.7), `L_full` ≈ 31 ms. Press at 8 ms (after frame k's driver step) or from a P5 handler at 6 ms: the tick runs in frame k+1 at ≈ 19.7 ms, drawn when that frame ends at 33.3 ms → `L_first` ≈ 25 ms, `L_full` ≈ 42 ms.

**D.5 Catch-up, simulated-time lag and forgiveness** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: integer accumulator owned by the `TickDriver` (CR-1a); forgiveness is part of the formula; the physics callback is not the clock)*

The `ticks_run_this_frame` formula is defined as:

`acc ← acc + delta_us × TICK_RATE`; `ticks_due = floor(acc / TICK_UNITS)`; `ticks_run = min(ticks_due, MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)` (fewer if the kernel leaves `RUNNING` inside the loop); `acc ← acc − ticks_run × TICK_UNITS`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| delta_us | int | 0–unbounded µs | injected into the `TickDriver` (the driver node converts the engine's `delta` once) | Wall time of the frame |
| TICK_UNITS | int | 1,000,000 | constant | Accumulator units per tick: the unit is microseconds × `TICK_RATE`, so a tick is exact for every integer `TICK_RATE` |
| acc | int | 0–unbounded | calculated (`TickDriver`) | Un-simulated time; **cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`** |
| ticks_due | int | 0–unbounded | calculated | Ticks that would keep sim time equal to wall time |
| MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME | int | 1–8 (default **4**) | data file | CR-17 catch-up cap |
| ticks_run | int | 0–4 | calculated | Ticks actually stepped this frame |

**Output Range:** 0 (a frame shorter than a tick) to `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`. Pure integer arithmetic: no float comparison, so no result depends on a fixture landing on a float boundary. The kernel's own `step()` has no accumulator; this lives in the driver, which needs no coupling to Godot's physics step cap.
**Example:** `delta_us = 100,000` at 60 Hz: `acc += 6,000,000` → `ticks_due = 6`, `ticks_run = 4`, `acc = 2,000,000` (2 ticks of lag).

The `lag_ticks` and forgiveness formula is defined as: *(Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), Open Question 19: `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0`, option B)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

`lag_ticks = floor(acc / TICK_UNITS)` after the frame's ticks; if `lag_ticks > LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` then `dropped = lag_ticks`, `acc ← acc mod TICK_UNITS` (the sub-tick remainder is kept so `tick_alpha` stays continuous), `lag_ticks ← 0`, the forgive counter and `dropped_ticks_total` increment — **at the end of the frame in which the threshold is exceeded**; `simulated_time_lag_s = lag_ticks × tick_duration`. At the ruled default `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0` this fires on every frame that ends with at least one whole tick of lag, so **no whole tick of lag ever survives into a later frame and the kernel never fast-forwards**. A non-zero value stays a parametric seam (tests exercise it as a fixture); it is not shipped.

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| lag_ticks | int | 0 after every frame at the default; 0–`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` after every frame in general | calculated | Exposed to diagnostics (CR-17); never exceeds the threshold after a frame (pre-forgiveness it can read up to `ticks_due − MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`) |
| LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS | int | 0–120 (default **0**, ruled 2026-10-27 — user ruling, Open Question 19) | data file | Lag above this is dropped, not repaid; 0 = every whole tick of lag is dropped |
| simulated_time_lag_s | float | 0 at the default; 0–`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` × `tick_duration` in general | calculated | How far the ship's clock is behind the player's |
| dropped_ticks_total | int | 0–unbounded | calculated | Diagnostics only |

**Output Range:** At the default, `lag_ticks == 0` after every frame, so the player never sees fast-forward: a frame that runs more than one tick does so only to cover wall time that elapsed within that one frame (at most `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`), never to repay lag from an earlier frame. Sustained frame times above `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME × tick_duration` (66.7 ms) run the sim at `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks per frame — slow motion, no spiral. Since no domain system reads wall time, dropped time is observable only in diagnostics. The earlier text allowed up to 30 ticks of sub-threshold lag to be repaid at up to 4× for up to 10 frames; that allowance is withdrawn. For a fixture with `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = N > 0` the most repayment is `N` ticks over `ceil(N / (MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME − 1))` frames.
**Example (default, hitch):** a 1.000 s hitch: `acc += 60,000,000` → `ticks_run = 4`, `lag_ticks = 56 > 0` → forgiven the same frame: `dropped = 56`, `lag_ticks = 0`, `acc = 0`; the next 16,667 µs frame (`acc = 1,000,020`) runs exactly 1 tick and leaves `acc = 20`.
**Example (default, mid-size hitch, off any tick boundary):** a 152 ms hitch (`delta_us = 152,000`): `acc = 9,120,000` → `ticks_due = 9`, `ticks_run = 4`, `acc = 5,120,000`, `lag_ticks = 5 > 0` → dropped: `dropped = 5`, `acc = 5,120,000 mod 1,000,000 = 120,000`, `lag_ticks = 0`. The next 16,667 µs frame: `acc = 1,120,020` → `ticks_run = 1`, `acc = 120,020`. No frame after the hitch runs more than 1 tick.
**Example (fixture only, `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 30`):** the same 152 ms hitch leaves `lag_ticks = 5 ≤ 30`, kept; following 16,667 µs frames add 1,000,020 units: `acc = 6,120,020` → `ticks_run = 4`, `lag_ticks = 2`; then `acc = 3,120,040` → `ticks_run = 3`, `lag_ticks = 0` — cleared in 2 further frames.

**D.6 Step budget**

TD-ADR: CONCERNS

ADR reviewed: C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--the-synaptic-sea-2d/e887ccb9-1186-40d9-9566-5eacccbd9b44/scratchpad/arch/adr-0001.draft.md (ADR-0001 Kernel Tick Driver and Frame Order, Proposed). Godot 4.7.2, domain Core.

## Summary verdict
The decision itself is sound. It follows the owner, command-simulation-layer.md CR-1a, D.3 and D.5, almost word for word. The problem statement is clear and the four alternatives are real; Alternative 2 (own `Time.get_ticks_usec` accumulator) is correctly kept as the spike fallback. The negative consequences are stated honestly. The engine version is stamped, and the unverified engine behaviours (cross-node `process_priority`, `Engine.time_scale`) are flagged and gated on KRN-LAT-02. I am not rejecting it. It still needs amendments before re-review. One is a gap in the interface plumbing, one is a code-level bug in the Decision text, one rule falls outside the ADR's scope and conflicts with two GDDs, and several citations are wrong. None of them changes the decision.

## A. Fix in the draft before re-review

1. **Presentation has no way to reach `tick_alpha` under injection (the § 4 and § 5 contradiction).** § 4 makes `tick_alpha` the clock value presentation reads. § 5 gives every module and subscriber only `setup(kernel: Kernel)`. Key Interfaces puts `tick_alpha` on `TickDriver`, which `KernelHost` holds, not `Kernel`. § 4 also says the value is not a block and the sim never reads it, so routing it through `Kernel` (as architecture.md's `Kernel.tick_alpha` example does, L524) cuts against the ADR's own framing. Decide one of these:
   - (a) a read-only presentation-clock facade injected next to the kernel, `setup(kernel, clock)`;
   - (b) the kernel exposes a non-hashed, non-persisted `clock` read view (the same pattern IC-5 uses for `restore_epoch`);
   - (c) keep only "injection, composition root, no autoload" here and hand the per-class injected type to ADR-0009 / ADR-0002.

   Related: handing the whole `Kernel` to every presentation subscriber gives presentation `submit()`, which architecture.md L427 limits to the INPUT_SURFACE handle. A universal `setup(kernel: Kernel)` pre-empts ADR-0002 (ingress handles) and ADR-0009 (what presentation may read). I recommend (c), plus one sentence saying the injected type per subscriber class is a narrow facet, not the full kernel.

2. **Integer-division bug in the `tick_alpha` formula.** § 4 and the diagram give `tick_alpha = clamp(acc / TICK_UNITS, 0.0, 1.0)`. `acc` and `TICK_UNITS` are both `int`, so in GDScript `acc / TICK_UNITS` is integer division and always gives 0 in normal running. Interpolation would never happen, and the project's `integer_division` warning policy (S0-a) would flag it. Write it as `clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0.0, 1.0)`. This text gets copied into stories, so it matters.

3. **The § 4 hold rule does not match D.3.** The ADR says `tick_alpha` is "held at 1 ... only transiently". D.3 (GDD L325-327) says two things:
   - the driver holds `tick_alpha` at 1.0 for the whole time the kernel is not `RUNNING`;
   - on every transition into `RUNNING`, the kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every `interpolated` block.

   Under the ADR's formula alone, a paused kernel would publish the frozen sub-tick remainder and draw a pose partway back toward the previous tick. D.3 explicitly forbids that. Restate both halves, or cite D.3 as binding for the non-`RUNNING` case.

4. **Wrong GDD anchors.** The Pipeline GDD only has rules PR-1 to PR-15 (grep of `**PR-n.`).
   - § 4 and the requirements table cite "PR-21, PR-22". The `present_time` owner is **PR-9** (pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md L209). PR-21 and PR-22 appear to be TR-pxl-021 and TR-pxl-022 mixed up with rule numbers.
   - The interpolation formula is credited to "Pipeline PR-5", which is the projection and draw-order rule. The formula is in Section D (L512), and the restore case is in Edge Cases (L786).

   Stories cite these anchors, so correct them.

5. **The § 6 / Implementation Guidelines rule "must never set `SceneTree.paused` in the MVP" is out of scope and conflicts with GDDs that are not in the sync list.**
   - architecture.md § Required ADRs gives ADR-0001 the tick source, priority order, `tick_alpha`, `present_time` and Adapter placement. Tree pause is not on that list.
   - chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md L257 and L504 send "kernel `PAUSED` vs `SceneTree.paused` / layer-3 `process_mode`" to its own ADR candidate (a), which belongs with ADR-0030 (UI framework / menus).
   - debug-overlay-true-values.md E-DO-48 (L833) and AC-DO-174 (L1377) assume `SceneTree.paused` *can* be true and test behaviour under it.

   My recommendation: ADR-0001 keeps what is in scope, that the driver is `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and kernel `PAUSED` is the only pause the simulation knows. Move the "never set it" rule and its lint to ADR-0030. If the author wants to keep the rule here, add Chart Table and Debug Overlay to § GDD sync and note that ADR-0001 absorbs Chart Table candidate (a).

6. **"The only wall-clock reads in the project" is stated too broadly.** § 1 and the clock-lint guideline say the `delta_us` conversion and the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads. But PR-9 says `present_time` "advances by the render delta" and the solver's smoothing reads `delta` (Pipeline L227), and Chart Table CT-43 (L483) keeps layer-3 accumulators driven by the render delta. Limit H9 to reads that reach the simulation, and say presentation may use its own `_process(delta)` for `present_time` and cosmetic clocks. Otherwise the lint's allow-list contradicts approved GDDs. Similarly, "`tick_alpha` is the only clock value presentation reads" should say "the only value presentation reads *from the driver*". PR-9 item 6 (L200) and LO-4 also let presentation read the committed `T` (for example `beacon_aim(T)`, LO-27).

## B. Fix before Acceptance (extend the Ordering Note / § GDD sync)

7. **More stale artifacts beyond the four GDDs.**
   - `docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md` TR-pc-004 (L287) still says "samples ... in the physics callback". TR-pxl-022 (L194) still names `physics_jitter_fix`. Stories embed TR IDs, so stale TR text is a worse hazard than stale prose. TR-cmd-004's (0)/(1)/(2) are ordinals and are fine.
   - architecture.md § Data Flow 1 (L259-275) labels priorities "0 / 1 / 2" as if they were values. It also lists `accumulator +=` *before* the boundary service. CR-1a says the boundary service runs first and a transition frame discards its own `delta_us`. OQ-1 (L716) repeats "process_priority 0 ... priority 1".
   - The Migration Plan only mentions the `Kernel.` global examples. Add Data Flow 1, OQ-1, OQ-13 and the L556 "ADR-0001 decides" paragraph to it.
   - The ADR's four-GDD list does match my grep for physics-callback text outside the kernel (PC L62/751/1021/1077, Suit L1441, Pipeline L227/297/1219, Assembly L1058/1161/1528/1593/1772/1940). Assembly L1528 and L1940 (open item 41) are missing from the ADR's list.

8. **IC-4 routing mismatch.** architecture.md IC-4 (L742) gives the `STEP_BUDGET_MS` semantics to ADR-0001. The ADR hands them to ADR-0003. The owner already settles it (an alarm at 4 ms, a P3 target of 2.0 ms), so either say that in one line here or record the move to ADR-0003 so the baseline and the ADR agree.

## C. Engine and enforcement notes (add to Verification Required or Risks; not blocking)

9. **One input-ordering claim is not verified.** The claim that `_input` / `_unhandled_input` are "delivered before the frame's `_process` calls" is stated as fact. The pinned reference does not cover it. Add it to KRN-LAT-02 alongside the priority-order check.
10. **Process thread groups.** `process_priority` ordering holds within a process group. A node with `process_thread_group` set to a sub-thread would leave the main-thread ordering, and would also break the main-thread rule. Add a lint or boot check that INPUT_SURFACE, KernelHost and presentation nodes use the default (main) thread group.
11. **Enforcing "never a literal `process_priority`".** Any `process_priority = n` in a `.tscn` is a literal by definition. State that scene files must not set it, and that code sets it from `ProcessPriority`. The authoritative check should be a boot-time tree walk: every node below `TICK_DRIVER` is a registered INPUT_SURFACE, and only `KernelHost` uses -50. A regex cannot see priorities set at runtime. Exactly how it is enforced is ADR-0010's call (OQ-16).
12. **Two settings the ADR does not mention.**
    - `application/run/delta_smoothing` (on by default in 4.x) reshapes `_process` delta.
    - From memory, without checking the engine reference: `MainTimerSync`'s jitter fix may also adjust the idle step, not just the physics step.

    Neither threatens determinism, because the sim only sees integer ticks and replays use tick-stamped streams. Both do affect the 0-tick/2-tick frame pattern and the latency numbers. State a position (leave both at default) and record the measured effect in the spike, rather than claiming the jitter fix has nothing to do with the tick.
13. **Validation greps.** "No `Kernel` autoload" must scan `project.godot` `[autoload]`, not `src/`. Also, the 100 ms hitch criterion is right: 6 due, 4 run, 2 dropped, `acc` = 0.

## D. Sound as drafted (record this so these points are not reopened)
- **Priority constants:** the -100 / -50 / 0 values, with `PRESENTATION` equal to the engine default, are the right safe-failure choice. Leaving gaps between the values is good. The three lint rules are enforceable, by a scene-file scan plus a boot walk. The 4.x `Node.process_priority` docs already say lower runs first, so the risk is low. ## Summary verdict
The decision itself is sound. It follows the owner, command-simulation-layer.md CR-1a, D.3 and D.5, almost word for word. The problem statement is clear and the four alternatives are real; Alternative 2 (own `Time.get_ticks_usec` accumulator) is correctly kept as the spike fallback. The negative consequences are stated honestly. The engine version is stamped, and the unverified engine behaviours (cross-node `process_priority`, `Engine.time_scale`) are flagged and gated on KRN-LAT-02. I am not rejecting it. It still needs amendments before re-review. One is a gap in the interface plumbing, one is a code-level bug in the Decision text, one rule falls outside the ADR's scope and conflicts with two GDDs, and several citations are wrong. None of them changes the decision.

## A. Fix in the draft before re-review

1. **Presentation has no way to reach `tick_alpha` under injection (the § 4 and § 5 contradiction).** § 4 makes `tick_alpha` the clock value presentation reads. § 5 gives every module and subscriber only `setup(kernel: Kernel)`. Key Interfaces puts `tick_alpha` on `TickDriver`, which `KernelHost` holds, not `Kernel`. § 4 also says the value is not a block and the sim never reads it, so routing it through `Kernel` (as architecture.md's `Kernel.tick_alpha` example does, L524) cuts against the ADR's own framing. Decide one of these:
   - (a) a read-only presentation-clock facade injected next to the kernel, `setup(kernel, clock)`;
   - (b) the kernel exposes a non-hashed, non-persisted `clock` read view (the same pattern IC-5 uses for `restore_epoch`);
   - (c) keep only "injection, composition root, no autoload" here and hand the per-class injected type to ADR-0009 / ADR-0002.

   Related: handing the whole `Kernel` to every presentation subscriber gives presentation `submit()`, which architecture.md L427 limits to the INPUT_SURFACE handle. A universal `setup(kernel: Kernel)` pre-empts ADR-0002 (ingress handles) and ADR-0009 (what presentation may read). I recommend (c), plus one sentence saying the injected type per subscriber class is a narrow facet, not the full kernel.

2. **Integer-division bug in the `tick_alpha` formula.** § 4 and the diagram give `tick_alpha = clamp(acc / TICK_UNITS, 0.0, 1.0)`. `acc` and `TICK_UNITS` are both `int`, so in GDScript `acc / TICK_UNITS` is integer division and always gives 0 in normal running. Interpolation would never happen, and the project's `integer_division` warning policy (S0-a) would flag it. Write it as `clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0.0, 1.0)`. This text gets copied into stories, so it matters.

3. **The § 4 hold rule does not match D.3.** The ADR says `tick_alpha` is "held at 1 ... only transiently". D.3 (GDD L325-327) says two things:
   - the driver holds `tick_alpha` at 1.0 for the whole time the kernel is not `RUNNING`;
   - on every transition into `RUNNING`, the kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every `interpolated` block.

   Under the ADR's formula alone, a paused kernel would publish the frozen sub-tick remainder and draw a pose partway back toward the previous tick. D.3 explicitly forbids that. Restate both halves, or cite D.3 as binding for the non-`RUNNING` case.

4. **Wrong GDD anchors.** The Pipeline GDD only has rules PR-1 to PR-15 (grep of `**PR-n.`).
   - § 4 and the requirements table cite "PR-21, PR-22". The `present_time` owner is **PR-9** (pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md L209). PR-21 and PR-22 appear to be TR-pxl-021 and TR-pxl-022 mixed up with rule numbers.
   - The interpolation formula is credited to "Pipeline PR-5", which is the projection and draw-order rule. The formula is in Section D (L512), and the restore case is in Edge Cases (L786).

   Stories cite these anchors, so correct them.

5. **The § 6 / Implementation Guidelines rule "must never set `SceneTree.paused` in the MVP" is out of scope and conflicts with GDDs that are not in the sync list.**
   - architecture.md § Required ADRs gives ADR-0001 the tick source, priority order, `tick_alpha`, `present_time` and Adapter placement. Tree pause is not on that list.
   - chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md L257 and L504 send "kernel `PAUSED` vs `SceneTree.paused` / layer-3 `process_mode`" to its own ADR candidate (a), which belongs with ADR-0030 (UI framework / menus).
   - debug-overlay-true-values.md E-DO-48 (L833) and AC-DO-174 (L1377) assume `SceneTree.paused` *can* be true and test behaviour under it.

   My recommendation: ADR-0001 keeps what is in scope, that the driver is `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and kernel `PAUSED` is the only pause the simulation knows. Move the "never set it" rule and its lint to ADR-0030. If the author wants to keep the rule here, add Chart Table and Debug Overlay to § GDD sync and note that ADR-0001 absorbs Chart Table candidate (a).

6. **"The only wall-clock reads in the project" is stated too broadly.** § 1 and the clock-lint guideline say the `delta_us` conversion and the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads. But PR-9 says `present_time` "advances by the render delta" and the solver's smoothing reads `delta` (Pipeline L227), and Chart Table CT-43 (L483) keeps layer-3 accumulators driven by the render delta. Limit H9 to reads that reach the simulation, and say presentation may use its own `_process(delta)` for `present_time` and cosmetic clocks. Otherwise the lint's allow-list contradicts approved GDDs. Similarly, "`tick_alpha` is the only clock value presentation reads" should say "the only value presentation reads *from the driver*". PR-9 item 6 (L200) and LO-4 also let presentation read the committed `T` (for example `beacon_aim(T)`, LO-27).

10. **Process thread groups.** `process_priority` ordering holds within a process group. A node with `process_thread_group` set to a sub-thread would leave the main-thread ordering, and would also break the main-thread rule. Add a lint or boot check that INPUT_SURFACE, KernelHost and presentation nodes use the default (main) thread group.
11. **Enforcing "never a literal `process_priority`".** Any `process_priority = n` in a `.tscn` is a literal by definition. The authoritative check should be a boot-time tree walk: every node below `TICK_DRIVER` is a registered INPUT_SURFACE, and only `KernelHost` uses -50. A regex cannot see priorities set at runtime. Exactly how it is enforced is ADR-0010's call (OQ-16).
